blocks.source: Vol IV, Supervisory Intervention, § The Authority Record
blocks.md: When an incident investigator asks, weeks after an abrupt blocked-aisle takeover, which entity drove the mobile base as it neared the rack end, the machine's recorded telemetry provides evidence bounded by its capture coverage, clock alignment, independent plant measurements, and trusted custody. The **authority record** bridges real-time supervisory arbitration with downstream verification and release claims. To establish this audit trail, the authority record consumes two upstream contracts.

questions.q: The section **The Authority Record** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: The authority record binds a sealed static authority manifest to a per-tick evidence tuple of time, authority state, measured state, proposed and admitted commands, so every handover is reconstructable and attributable.
Automation leaves the human the hardest, least-time cases with degraded skill and a stale forward model, so oversight degrades exactly when it is needed.
A remote assistant is admitted only if reaction budget, handshake latency, manual lease, and blend window fit the remaining clearance, and remote assistance is never a safety layer.
Takeover latency (sensory, cognitive, motor, console) is long-tailed and must be budgeted at a design percentile as a delay before braking, which sets the speed a supervised machine may run.
